component.name: Weir
component.summary: Mix and route microphones and applications

description.p: Weir puts the sound on your computer on a mixing desk, in the style of Voicemeeter. Your microphone, your music, your browser and your game each get a strip with a fader. Your headphones, your speakers and a virtual microphone for Discord or OBS each get a bus. A row of buttons beside every fader decides who hears what.

ul.li: As many strips and buses as you need, each a device other programs can choose
A separate mix for every output, so a strip can be louder in your headphones than on your stream
Noise suppression, a noise gate, a compressor and a 16-band equalizer for voices
Ducking, which turns the music down while you talk, and a safety limiter on every output
Scenes, setups, rules for where applications go, and undo
A command line and a documented protocol, for scripts and stream decks

screenshot.caption: The mixer: strips on the left, buses on the right
A strip's noise gate, compressor and equalizer

description.p: Weir is now also packaged for Arch Linux and the systems built on it, and for Fedora and Nobara on COPR. Weir itself is unchanged.
